Subject: Recap + next steps from demo — perf SLOs & benchmark exchange

Hi Alice / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can validate Redwood against EdgeFin's perf SLOs: 

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Latency targets: p95 generation latency <= 250ms for 1k-token responses (streaming enabled)
- Throughput: baseline 100 QPS for short-form use (avg 200 tokens), spike to 300 QPS for batch windows
- Concurrency: expected 50 concurrent active streams for the core trading-alert workflow
- Streaming: required (server-sent events) with token-by-token delivery and low tail latency

What we'd like to exchange:
1) Our benchmark methodology and measurement definitions (what we measure, environment, kernels).
2) Your representative prompt set and traffic mix (we discussed a 70/20/10 split: short/medium/long).
3) Any SRE constraints (VPC egress rules, TLS mutual auth) that affect test harness.

Next steps (proposed):
- I will send our benchmark methodology doc and the sample prompt CSV. (Action: Marissa, today)
- Rishi to propose a reproducible harness (Docker-compose or k8s job) and measurement checklist. (Action: Rishi, by Mon)
- EdgeFin to confirm one representative dataset and preferred region to run tests. (Action: Alice/Samir, by Wed)

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_methodology_v1.pdf, edgefin_prompt_set_v1.csv (see below).

If anything above is off, call it out and I’ll update. Otherwise, we’ll plan to run an initial benchmark in our us-west region next week and share raw logs.

Thanks —
Marissa

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap — this matches our notes. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The 250ms p95 is for interactive workflows (short-form alerts). For longer-form analysis jobs we have a looser target (p95 < 800ms) but those can run on a different route.
- Concurrency of 50 is the steady-state target; we have planned burst windows up to 120 concurrent streams during market opens. If you can test both steady and burst that'd be ideal.
- We absolutely need token-level streaming with no more than 10ms added jitter per token compared to non-streaming baseline.

We’ll drop a representative prompt sample into the CSV you attached and confirm region preference (likely us-west). Will also share SRE contact info for firewall testing.

Alice

Marissa / team —

Attached is the first-pass of the harness notes and measurement checklist. High-level notes:
- Measurement definitions: we’ll report p50/p90/p95/p99 for both latency-to-first-byte (TTFB) and end-to-end token latency. For streaming, we’ll also report per-token inter-arrival jitter distribution and tail percentiles.
- Environment: reproducible Docker image + compose file that runs a load-generator (wrk + custom stream driver) against a pinned model variant. We’ll capture raw traces and kernel-level stats.
- Workloads: 3 mixes — short (70%), medium (20%), long (10%) using the CSV prompts Marissa attached. We’ll include steady-state and burst schedules (50 -> 120 concurrency over 60s).
- Reproducibility: we’ll publish a terraform + docker-compose recipe and seed rng where applicable; results will include exact machine types, kernel versions, model commit hashes, quantization profile.

I attached: perf_harness_docker_instructions.txt and updated methodology PDF (v1.1 inline notes). I’ll sync with Vivek on kernel selection and any engine flags we should surface.

Questions for EdgeFin: do you have a deterministic dataset for the long-form analysis jobs (we need a stable evaluation corpus)? Also, confirm whether TLS mutual auth is required for the test endpoint.

—Rishi
